body.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\), determine the smallest deterministic penalty sequence \(\ell_n\ge1\) for which a fully data-driven estimator and confidence interval, not given \(\kappa\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), or \(r_{en}\), attain uniform risk and honest expected length at most \(C\ell_n\rho_n\) over compact ranges of these indices; prove a matching adaptation lower bound for \(\ell_n\).
body.justification: The oracle frontier identifies the scales that a data-driven procedure would need to learn but does not make the deterministic global prediction-error certificates observable.
body.gap: Existing data-driven trimming or conditional ERM results do not identify the smallest joint adaptation penalty for the four ATE channels when the shell index, shell constants, and all public-function radii are unknown.
body.consumer: Resolving the question would determine whether the oracle clipping and honest-interval benchmarks are implementable without a logarithmic or polynomial adaptation loss.

obligation.what_is_open: The smallest adaptation penalty and its matching lower bound when the tail exponent, both shell constants, and all three nuisance radii are unknown.
obligation.obstruction: The oracle threshold depends on three competing unknown scales.  The frozen adaptation handle supplies neither observable upper confidence bounds for the global approximation errors nor a between-class testing construction.  Under the frozen model, validation data do not uniformly identify the deterministic public-predictor errors, so neither the oracle clipping bias nor the radius of an honest interval can be selected uniformly from the sample.
obligation.attempted: A dyadic Lepski comparison controls stochastic differences among clipped scores, but its deterministic biases contain \(r_{1n}\lambda^{\kappa/2}\), \(r_{1n}r_{en}/\lambda\), and \(r_{0n}r_{en}\), none of which has an observable uniform upper certificate in the frozen model.  Empirical shell counts also require control of the unknown propensity approximation error, which is itself one of the quantities being adapted to.
obligation.partial_result: When \(\kappa\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), and the certified radii are supplied, thm:clipped-absolute-upper, lem:median-risk-upgrade, and thm:honest-interval-frontier attain risk and honest expected length of order \(\rho_n\); hence the oracle adaptation penalty equals \(1\).  The frozen primitives imply no uniform unknown-index penalty.
